## Pros

- Toddler seat approved from birth to 50 lb with no add-on ([US manual 260710](https://back.uppababy.com/media/2d/bd/8a/1790001116/NA_2201-KNA_KonaManual_260710_a11y.pdf)).
- UPPAbaby sells it as a Kona + Aria V2 bundle; the seat "attaches directly" ([bundle page](https://uppababy.com/bundles/travel-systems/kona-aria-v2-travel-system), [help centre 2026-09-25](https://support.uppababy.com/hc/en-us/articles/43763742563607)).
- Lighter than the Cruz V3 and Vista V3 (22 lb, [maker](https://uppababy.com/strollers/full-size/kona/james/)); folds with the seat on either way; [travel bag](https://uppababy.com/accessories/strollers-accessories/kona-travel-bag/) needs no wheel removal ($149.99).

## Cons

Misuse risks come first.

- **Misuse risk:** no manual describes attaching the Aria V2 to the Kona or checking it. The [Kona manual](https://back.uppababy.com/media/2d/bd/8a/1790001116/NA_2201-KNA_KonaManual_260710_a11y.pdf) has no car seat section, and the [Aria V2 manual](https://back.prod.uppababy.com/media/4b/51/e9/1794583326/US-EN_1002-ARI_AriaV2Manual_260724.pdf) (rev. 260724) does not list the Kona.
- **Misuse risk:** UPPAbaby's [bundle page](https://uppababy.com/bundles/travel-systems/kona-aria-v2-travel-system) says the carrier can face outward on the Kona; the [Aria V2 manual](https://back.prod.uppababy.com/media/4b/51/e9/1794583326/US-EN_1002-ARI_AriaV2Manual_260724.pdf) allows parent-facing only.
- Ride over bumps is "good, but not great", rougher than the Cruz and Vista ([Babylist](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/best-strollers)); seat sits low and the handlebar wobbles when fully extended.
- Fold gets stuck for some owners (low confidence); no measured weight or fold; only one hands-on write-up ([usability note](../../research/notes/2026-11-28-uppababy-full-size-usability.md)).
- Does not fit the 22 x 14 x 9 in overhead bin ([specs note](../../research/notes/2026-11-28-uppababy-strollers-specs-and-gates.md)).
